adventure.title: Cyclone at Coney Island
adventure.description: The 1927 wooden roller coaster at Luna Park is still running — buy a ride, eat a Nathan's hot dog, walk the boardwalk in the off-season when it belongs to locals.
adventure.bonus: Ride the Cyclone twice in a row without getting off.

adventure.title: Yankee Stadium Bleacher Creatures
adventure.description: Section 203 in right field — the Bleacher Creatures run roll call at the start of every game, every player acknowledges them, and the cheap ticket is the right ticket.
adventure.bonus: Learn the roll call chant before you go and participate from the first pitch.

adventure.title: 9/11 Memorial Before 9am
adventure.description: The twin reflecting pools on a weekday morning before the crowds — the names on the bronze parapets, the survivor tree, the sound of the waterfalls. Go quiet.
adventure.bonus: Find a name on the memorial from your hometown.

adventure.title: Lower Manhattan Night Ghost Tour
adventure.description: A 90-minute walk through FiDi, Tribeca, and the Financial District — the stories are half myth, but the neighborhood is 400 years old and doesn't need embellishment.
adventure.bonus: Try to debunk one story on the tour by looking it up after.

adventure.title: NYC Ferry — All Five Lines in One Day
adventure.description: Board at Pier 11 in FiDi and ride all five NYC Ferry routes — Astoria, East River, South Brooklyn, Rockaway, St. George — the best $3.50 transportation deal in the city.
adventure.bonus: Document the full circuit — photo at every terminal you stop at.

adventure.title: One World Trade Observatory at Dusk
adventure.description: Book the FLEX ticket 30 minutes before sunset and stay for the city lighting up below — the only right way to do this is at dusk, never at noon.
adventure.bonus: Identify five landmarks on all four sides without using the interactive displays.

chill.title: Socrates Sculpture Park
chill.description: The free outdoor sculpture park on the Long Island City waterfront puts large-scale art against the full Manhattan skyline — always changing, always worth the 7 train.
chill.bonus: Photograph one piece and write one sentence about what you think it means.

chill.title: NYPL Rose Main Reading Room
chill.description: The Beaux-Arts reading room at 42nd Street — 78 feet of painted ceiling, long oak tables, total silence — get a free day pass and do nothing productive for two hours.
chill.bonus: Bring a physical book, not a laptop — read for the full two hours.

chill.title: The Strand Dollar Carts on Broadway
chill.description: The outdoor $1 carts in front of The Strand at 12th and Broadway — spend $10 on six strange books, take your time, no rush and no one's watching.
chill.bonus: Buy one book you know nothing about based only on the cover.

chill.title: MoMA PS1 Courtyard
chill.description: The Long Island City contemporary art satellite's courtyard often outperforms the galleries — check their Warm Up summer DJ series on Saturdays.
chill.bonus: Find one piece that genuinely unsettles you and sit with it for five minutes.

chill.title: Metrograph Cinema on Ludlow St
chill.description: The LES arthouse theater with a serious programming calendar — the cafe is great, the projection is better, and they always have something showing nobody else is playing.
chill.bonus: Pick a film you know nothing about — choose by the poster only.

chill.title: Brooklyn Heights Promenade at Dusk
chill.description: The elevated esplanade above the BQE holds the most complete lower Manhattan skyline view in the city — the 30 minutes before sunset makes the whole thing golden.
chill.bonus: Bring a film camera — no phone photos.

chill.title: Inwood Hill Park — Manhattan's Last Forest
chill.description: Manhattan's last old-growth forest at the island's northern tip — ancient caves, herons on the Harlem River, not a tourist in sight; take the A to Inwood-207th St.
chill.bonus: Find the plaque marking where Peter Minuit bought Manhattan from the Lenape.

chill.title: Green-Wood Cemetery Walk
chill.description: The 478-acre National Historic Landmark in Brooklyn — Gothic chapel, glacial ponds, Victorian monuments — the most peaceful walk in the outer boroughs.
chill.bonus: Find a grave belonging to someone you've actually heard of — the list is longer than you think.

foodie.title: Zabar's Saturday Morning Circuit
foodie.description: The Upper West Side institution on Broadway — smoked sable, whitefish salad, a sesame bagel, eaten standing on the sidewalk like the regulars do.
foodie.bonus: Find one ingredient in the store you've never cooked with and buy it.

foodie.title: Levain Bakery Cookie — Original Location
foodie.description: The original Upper West Side bakery on 74th Street — get the walnut chocolate chip warm and eat it on the sidewalk while it's still hot.
foodie.bonus: Pair it with a coffee from a different cafe on the same block.

foodie.title: Red Rooster Harlem Brunch
foodie.description: Marcus Samuelsson's Harlem cornerstone on Lenox Ave delivers cornbread, a Bird's Eye cocktail, and a room that feels like the neighborhood itself.
foodie.bonus: Stay for the Sunday gospel brunch and tip the musicians separately.

foodie.title: Smorgasburg Williamsburg Saturday
foodie.description: 100 local food vendors on the Williamsburg waterfront every Saturday with the Manhattan skyline behind them — bring cash and two hours.
foodie.bonus: Try three things you've never eaten before and rank them honestly.

foodie.title: Katz's Deli Pastrami at Midnight
foodie.description: The pastrami on rye at midnight hits differently when the tourists are gone and the regulars claim the tables — order a full stack, extra mustard, no negotiation.
foodie.bonus: Eat your entire sandwich standing at the counter like a local.

foodie.title: Sylvia's Harlem Soul Food
foodie.description: The Harlem institution on Lenox Ave — fried chicken, collard greens, candied yams, and cornbread in a room that's hosted every kind of person.
foodie.bonus: Come for the Sunday gospel brunch and arrive 15 minutes early.

foodie.title: Di Fara Pizza in Midwood
foodie.description: Dom DeMarco's family still runs the counter in Brooklyn's Midwood — one slice of the regular pie, one square, accept the wait, pay cash, eat at the counter.
foodie.bonus: Introduce yourself to the person next to you in line — the wait gives you time.

foodie.title: Ivan Ramen Counter on Clinton St
foodie.description: Rich, clean shio ramen from the American chef who earned his stripes in Tokyo — sit at the counter, order the Six Mushroom Ramen, and watch the kitchen.
foodie.bonus: Eat at the counter solo, no phone — watch the kitchen the entire time.

foodie.title: Nom Wah Tea Parlor Dim Sum
foodie.description: NYC's oldest dim sum parlor (est. 1920) on Doyers Street — egg rolls and steamed rice rolls, eaten slowly with hot oolong at a table that's seen a century of the city.
foodie.bonus: Order one thing from the menu you've never tried — no phone translation allowed.

foodie.title: Russ & Daughters Sunday Lox Plate
foodie.description: Order the Classic at the Orchard Street sit-down — hand-sliced Nova, cream cheese, capers, red onion on a perfect bagel — before the line wraps the block.
foodie.bonus: Order the Gaspe Nova instead of the regular and taste the difference.

active.title: Arthur Avenue Italian Market, Bronx
active.description: The real Little Italy in the Bronx — Biancardi's meat market, Borgatti's fresh pasta, Madonia Brothers bakery — bring a cooler and shop like you live here.
active.bonus: Cook a full Italian dinner with only what you buy on this one block.

active.title: Flushing Main St Soup Dumpling Crawl
active.description: The Golden Shopping Mall underground food court for soup dumplings and hand-pulled noodles, then White Bear for wontons — the best block of eating in all of Queens.
active.bonus: Order using a translation app — the counter staff will appreciate the effort.

active.title: Prospect Park Long Loop Run
active.description: The 3.35-mile perimeter loop through Brooklyn's Olmsted-designed park, closed to cars all weekend — enter at Grand Army Plaza, run counterclockwise, finish at the boathouse.
active.bonus: Run it twice and spot something different on the second lap.

active.title: Rockaway Beach A-Train Day Trip
active.description: The A train to Far Rockaway drops you at a real city beach with real waves — in summer the food trucks line the lot, in fall you have it mostly to yourself.
active.bonus: Swim past the break and float on your back looking at the city skyline.

active.title: Hudson River Kayak Tour
active.description: Manhattan Kayak Co. runs guided tours from Pier 66 — the city from the water, paddle in hand, is a completely different place than the city from the street.
active.bonus: Kayak close enough to read the name of a passing boat.

active.title: Jackson Heights Food Walk
active.description: Start at Roosevelt Ave and 74th St in Queens — Colombian bakeries, Nepali momos, Indian sweets, Ecuadorian ceviche — the most densely diverse square mile on Earth.
active.bonus: Eat food from five different countries and name them all without googling.

active.title: Industry City Wander, Sunset Park
active.description: The converted industrial complex in Sunset Park has glassblowing studios, a Japanese grocer, a whiskey distillery, specialty coffee, and woodworking workshops all on one campus.
active.bonus: Watch a craftsperson at work and describe what they're making to someone else in your group.

active.title: Hudson River Greenway Full Ride
active.description: Citi Bike from Pier 84 at 44th St north to Dyckman — 12 miles of separated path along the Hudson, mostly flat, views the whole way, coffee stop at 125th.
active.bonus: Ride it in under 90 minutes, stopping only for the coffee.

social.title: House of Yes Themed Night
social.description: The Bushwick arts collective runs themed nights every weekend — acrobats, aerialists, the most committed costume crowd in NYC, and DJs who actually read the room.
social.bonus: Come in full costume for the theme — no half-measures at House of Yes.

social.title: Employees Only Midnight Kitchen
social.description: The West Village cocktail bar behind the neon psychic sign keeps the kitchen open until 3:30am on weekends — get a Billionaire's Margarita and the bone marrow.
social.bonus: Get there before midnight and stay until after 2am — the room changes completely.

social.title: Please Don't Tell (PDT) Speakeasy
social.description: Enter through the phone booth in Crif Dogs on St. Marks — call ahead, max 45 people, cocktails that justify the ritual every single time.
social.bonus: Order something not on the menu by describing your mood to the bartender.

social.title: Dead Rabbit Cocktail Bar
social.description: The FiDi bar ranked among the world's best takes Irish pub history seriously — go upstairs to the Parlor, order a punch, and read the cocktail menu like a short story.
social.bonus: Ask the bartender to recommend something that's not on the menu.

social.title: Koreatown Karaoke Night
social.description: Book a private room at Gagopa or Turntable on 32nd Street after midnight — Korean karaoke rooms are cheaper, louder, and more fun than anything Midtown deserves.
social.bonus: Everyone has to sing one song they've never sung before.

social.title: Berg'n Beer Hall Bocce
social.description: The Crown Heights beer hall has a bocce court, rotating local food vendors, all-draft beer, and zero attitude — exactly the Saturday spot Brooklyn promises but rarely delivers.
social.bonus: Challenge strangers to bocce — the crowd here always says yes.

social.title: Westlight Rooftop, Williamsburg
social.description: The William Vale Hotel rooftop in Williamsburg gives you the full Manhattan skyline from across the river — the view from Brooklyn looking back is better than anything from Midtown.
social.bonus: Get there for the last 30 minutes of sunset and stay for the city lights.

social.title: Blue & Gold Tavern Pinball
social.description: The East Village dive bar with vintage pinball machines, $5 beers, and regulars who've been coming since before it was cool to be here.
social.bonus: Whoever scores lowest on pinball buys the next round.
